scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
administering_body: National Health Authority (NHA), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
target_beneficiaries: Bottom ~40% economically vulnerable families identified per SECC 2011 deprivation/occupational criteria (state-specific extensions vary); since Sept 2024, all senior citizens aged 70+ regardless of income (Vay Vandana top-up)
coverage_amount_summary: Rs 5 lakh per family per year, family floater, cashless and paperless; additional Rs 5 lakh top-up cover for citizens aged 70+ (separate from family cover), approved by Union Cabinet Sept 2024
empanelled_hospitals_summary: 30,000+ empanelled public and private hospitals nationwide (network size fluctuates; treat as approximate)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation (NHA/MoHFW press material summarized by secondary sources; no direct .gov.in fetch this session)
notes: Largest govt-funded health assurance scheme globally by beneficiary count. Operates in convergence with several state schemes (see Telangana and Andhra Pradesh rows) rather than replacing them. Exact current empanelled-hospital count and beneficiary-family count should be re-verified against the live NHA dashboard when direct fetch is possible.

administering_body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (Directorate General of CGHS)
target_beneficiaries: Serving and retired central government employees and their dependent family members; also covers some autonomous body employees, MPs, ex-MPs, Members of specified categories, and journalists in certain cities per separate orders
coverage_amount_summary: No fixed monetary ceiling; cashless treatment at CGHS package rates covering OPD, IPD/hospitalization, diagnostics, and AYUSH systems; FY2025-26 CGHS budget reported at approx. Rs 2,370 crore
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Approx. 2,486 empanelled private hospitals/diagnostic centres plus all CGHS wellness centres and government hospitals across roughly 80 covered cities
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing MoHFW/CGHS material via secondary sources
notes: IMPORTANT DOMAIN CHANGE: legacy domains cghs.gov.in and cghs.nic.in were deactivated on 28 April 2025 when a new unified CGHS Digital Platform/HMIS went live; cghs.mohfw.gov.in is now the only current official portal. Beneficiary count cited in secondary sources ranges 42-50 lakh depending on source/date; treat exact figure as PENDING_VERIFICATION.

administering_body: Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
target_beneficiaries: Employees earning up to Rs 21,000/month (Rs 25,000/month for persons with disabilities) in establishments with 10+ employees (varies by state) covered under the ESI Act, plus their dependents
coverage_amount_summary: No fixed ceiling on medical treatment cost (full medical care from day one of employment); cash benefits include sickness benefit at 70% of wages (up to 91 days/year, extendable up to 2 years at 80% for 34 specified long-term illnesses), disability benefit at ~90% of wages, and maternity benefit at 100% of wages; post-retirement/permanent-disability medical care continues for a nominal annual fee (reported ~Rs 120)
empanelled_hospitals_summary: ESI hospitals and dispensaries network across 668 notified districts (565 fully notified + 103 partially notified) in 36 states/UTs
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing ESIC official material via secondary sources
notes: Wage-ceiling and district-notification figures should be periodically re-checked as they are revised by government notification from time to time.

administering_body: Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, Ministry of Defence, Government of India (Central Organisation ECHS, headed by a Managing Director)
target_beneficiaries: Retired Armed Forces personnel (ex-servicemen) drawing pension, and their dependents (spouse, dependent unemployed/unmarried/divorced/widowed daughters, dependent sons up to 25 years, handicapped children, dependent parents)
coverage_amount_summary: Generally no fixed monetary ceiling on cost of treatment; covers OPD consultation, hospitalization, diagnostics, surgeries, medicines, and specialist care at no direct cost to the veteran; one-time contribution required at enrollment (amount varies by rank/category, not independently verified this session)
empanelled_hospitals_summary: 427+ ECHS polyclinics plus service/military hospitals and empanelled civil/private hospitals nationwide
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing DESW/ECHS official material via secondary sources
notes: Scheme approved 30 Dec 2002, launched 1 Apr 2003. One-time contribution/subscription amount by rank not independently verified this session; mark as PENDING_VERIFICATION if that figure is required downstream.

administering_body: Aarogyasri Health Care Trust, Health, Medical and Family Welfare Department, Government of Telangana
target_beneficiaries: Originally Below Poverty Line (BPL)/white-ration-card households; the Dec 2023 relaunch broadened intent toward wider population coverage, and in May 2025 the scheme was extended to orphans (full coverage without fresh means-testing); operates in convergence with AB PM-JAY
coverage_amount_summary: Rs 10 lakh per family per year (doubled from a prior Rs 5 lakh ceiling under the government formed in Dec 2023); in July 2024 the government added 163 new medical procedures to the package, of which 98 are funded/covered via AB-PMJAY convergence and 65 are state-funded
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Empanelled network of government and private hospitals under Aarogyasri Health Care Trust across Telangana (exact current count not independently verified this session)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing Telangana govt announcements via news and secondary sources
notes: RENAME/CHANGE FOUND: previously operated simply as 'Aarogyasri' (originally 'Rajiv Aarogyasri' at 2007 launch under undivided AP, later just 'Aarogyasri' in Telangana); the Congress-led government under CM A. Revanth Reddy (sworn in Dec 2023) relaunched it as 'Rajiv Aarogyasri' with the coverage increase to Rs 10 lakh, effective 9 Dec 2023. Distinct from the Telangana Employees Health Scheme/NEHS (see separate row), which covers only government employees/pensioners rather than the general BPL population.

scheme_name: New Employees Health Scheme (NEHS) [formerly Employees Health Scheme / EHS Telangana]
administering_body: Employees Health Care Trust (EHCT), Government of Telangana (newly constituted trust headed by the Chief Secretary, with 17 government representatives, 10 employee representatives, and 3 pensioner representatives)
target_beneficiaries: Telangana state government employees, service pensioners, family pensioners, and their eligible dependent family members (reported ~17.88 lakh beneficiaries: ~4.39 lakh employees, ~3.62 lakh pensioners, ~9.88 lakh dependents)
coverage_amount_summary: Cashless treatment with no prescribed upper financial ceiling stated for approved treatment; 1,816 medical and surgical packages aligned with CGHS package rates
empanelled_hospitals_summary: 114 government hospitals plus 886 empanelled private hospitals and wellness centres, including major chains (Apollo, Yashoda, KIMS, Medicover, Kamineni, Continental, CARE, Star, Basavatarakam)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation of contemporaneous news coverage (launch-week reporting)
notes: VERY RECENT RENAME/RESTRUCTURE: NEHS was launched 17 July 2026 (four days before this collection date), replacing the earlier Employees Health Scheme (EHS) which had been administered via the Aarogyasri Health Care Trust's hospital network. A dedicated new Employees Health Care Trust (EHCT) now administers it, with a formal trust deed unveiled at launch. Because this change is only days old, corroboration is currently limited to launch-week news coverage rather than settled reference sources; confidence capped accordingly. Re-verify beneficiary/hospital counts and portal stability in a future collection cycle.

scheme_name: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Scheme [formerly Dr. YSR Aarogyasri]
administering_body: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust (formally Dr. Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao Vaidya Seva Trust), Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, Government of Andhra Pradesh
target_beneficiaries: Below Poverty Line (BPL) families and families with annual income up to Rs 5 lakh in Andhra Pradesh
coverage_amount_summary: Cashless treatment up to Rs 25 lakh per eligible family per year: the first Rs 2.5 lakh of approved treatment cost is covered via an insurance company, with expenses beyond Rs 2.5 lakh up to Rs 25 lakh borne directly by the Trust; approx. 3,257 approved medical/surgical procedures across 31 super-speciality categories; scheme is integrated with AB PM-JAY
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Network of government and empanelled private hospitals under the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust across Andhra Pradesh (exact current count not independently verified this session)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing AP govt/health department material via secondary sources
notes: CONFIRMED RENAME: this scheme has changed names repeatedly with changes of government - launched 2007 as 'Rajiv Aarogyasri' under YSR Congress founder Dr Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy; renamed 'NTR Aarogya Seva'/'NTR Vaidya Seva' under TDP (from 2014); renamed 'Dr. YSR Aarogyasri' in 2019 under YSRCP (CM Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy); renamed again to 'Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva' in July 2024 after the TDP-led NDA coalition (CM N. Chandrababu Naidu) took office. The administering trust was correspondingly renamed from 'Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust' to 'Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust'. The Rs 25 lakh coverage figure and Rs 2.5 lakh insurance-company threshold appear consistently across multiple secondary sources but were not confirmed against a primary .gov.in document this session; treat as high-confidence but not certainty.

administering_body: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust (administering trust renamed July 2024 from Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust; scheme name 'EHS' itself was not renamed), Government of Andhra Pradesh
target_beneficiaries: Current and retired Andhra Pradesh state government employees and their dependent family members
coverage_amount_summary: Cashless inpatient and outpatient treatment, hospital stays, and follow-up/chronic-disease care, replacing the earlier medical-reimbursement process; PENDING_VERIFICATION - exact current per-family monetary ceiling not confirmed against a primary source this session (secondary sources are inconsistent or omit a specific figure)
empanelled_hospitals_summary: Network of empanelled hospitals shared with the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust network across Andhra Pradesh (exact current count not independently verified this session)
data_source: WebSearch aggregation summarizing secondary/aggregator sources; several aggregator sites still reference the pre-2024 trust name
notes: NAME NUANCE: unlike the BPL-facing scheme (Dr YSR Aarogyasri -> Dr NTR Vaidya Seva), the employee-facing 'EHS' scheme brand name itself does not appear to have changed in 2024; only its administering trust was renamed. Multiple aggregator/secondary sources have not updated to reflect the July 2024 trust rename and still say 'Dr YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust' - flagged here as a known lag in secondary sources, not necessarily a fact error. Coverage ceiling figure needs verification against ehs.ap.gov.in or a G.O. when direct fetch is possible.
